laws.historical_context: The Lebanese Code of Labour was enacted on 23 September 1946, shortly after Lebanon's independence. It remains the primary legislation governing employment relationships in Lebanon, covering individual and collective labor relations, working conditions, wages, termination, and labor disputes. Major amendments have been introduced over the decades, but the core framework remains in force.

key_articles.title: Scope of Application
key_articles.content: The present Code shall apply to all employers and employees in Lebanon, subject to the exceptions provided herein. It governs the relations between employers and employees and defines their respective rights and obligations arising from employment contracts.
key_articles.text_english: Scope of Application: The present Code shall apply to all employers and employees in Lebanon, subject to the exceptions provided herein. It governs the relations between employers and employees and defines their respective rights and obligations arising from employment contracts.
key_articles.subject: Scope of Application

key_articles.title: Definition of Employer
key_articles.content: An employer is any person, natural or juridical, who in an industrial, trading, or agricultural enterprise employs a worker in some capacity under a contract of employment, whether written or verbal.
key_articles.text_english: Definition of Employer: An employer is any person, natural or juridical, who in an industrial, trading, or agricultural enterprise employs a worker in some capacity under a contract of employment, whether written or verbal.
key_articles.subject: Definition of Employer

key_articles.title: Definition of Employee
key_articles.content: An employee is any person who undertakes, in return for remuneration, to work under the direction and supervision of another person, whether the contract is for a fixed or indefinite period.
key_articles.text_english: Definition of Employee: An employee is any person who undertakes, in return for remuneration, to work under the direction and supervision of another person, whether the contract is for a fixed or indefinite period.
key_articles.subject: Definition of Employee

key_articles.title: Exclusions from Application
key_articles.content: The following are excluded from the scope of this Code: domestic servants and persons employed in family enterprises where only members of the family are employed. Agricultural workers are governed by special provisions.
key_articles.text_english: Exclusions from Application: The following are excluded from the scope of this Code: domestic servants and persons employed in family enterprises where only members of the family are employed. Agricultural workers are governed by special provisions.
key_articles.subject: Exclusions from Application

key_articles.title: Written and Oral Contracts
key_articles.content: The contract of labor can be either oral or written; if written, it must be in Arabic. It may however be translated into a foreign language if one of the parties does not understand Arabic.
key_articles.text_english: Written and Oral Contracts: The contract of labor can be either oral or written; if written, it must be in Arabic. It may however be translated into a foreign language if one of the parties does not understand Arabic.
key_articles.subject: Written and Oral Contracts

key_articles.title: Types of Employment Contracts
key_articles.content: Employment contracts may be for a determined or undetermined duration. A contract for a determined duration must specify the period or the completion of a specific task. If the parties continue to perform after the expiry of a fixed-term contract, it shall be deemed renewed for an indefinite period.
key_articles.text_english: Types of Employment Contracts: Employment contracts may be for a determined or undetermined duration. A contract for a determined duration must specify the period or the completion of a specific task. If the parties continue to perform after the expiry of a fixed-term contract, it shall be deemed renewed for an indefinite period.
key_articles.subject: Types of Employment Contracts

key_articles.title: Trial Period
key_articles.content: The employment contract may provide for a trial period not exceeding three months. During this period, either party may terminate the contract without notice or indemnity. If the employee is retained beyond the trial period, the duration of the trial shall be counted as part of the service period.
key_articles.text_english: Trial Period: The employment contract may provide for a trial period not exceeding three months. During this period, either party may terminate the contract without notice or indemnity. If the employee is retained beyond the trial period, the duration of the trial shall be counted as part of the service period.
key_articles.subject: Trial Period

key_articles.title: Establishments Subject to the Code
key_articles.content: This Code applies to industrial, commercial, and agricultural establishments, as well as to enterprises providing services, public utility companies, liberal professions, associations, and other entities employing workers under conditions of subordination.
key_articles.text_english: Establishments Subject to the Code: This Code applies to industrial, commercial, and agricultural establishments, as well as to enterprises providing services, public utility companies, liberal professions, associations, and other entities employing workers under conditions of subordination.
key_articles.subject: Establishments Subject to the Code

key_articles.title: Maximum Working Hours
key_articles.content: The maximum working hours shall be 48 hours per week. The employer shall organize working hours within this limit. Working hours may be distributed over six days or reduced to five days with corresponding longer daily hours, provided the daily maximum does not exceed the limits set by regulation.
key_articles.text_english: Maximum Working Hours: The maximum working hours shall be 48 hours per week. The employer shall organize working hours within this limit. Working hours may be distributed over six days or reduced to five days with corresponding longer daily hours, provided the daily maximum does not exceed the limits set by regulation.
key_articles.subject: Maximum Working Hours

key_articles.title: Overtime Compensation
key_articles.content: Work performed beyond the normal working hours shall be compensated at a rate of at least 50% above the normal wage rate. Work performed on weekly rest days or public holidays shall be compensated at double the normal rate.
key_articles.text_english: Overtime Compensation: Work performed beyond the normal working hours shall be compensated at a rate of at least 50% above the normal wage rate. Work performed on weekly rest days or public holidays shall be compensated at double the normal rate.
key_articles.subject: Overtime Compensation

key_articles.title: Night Work Restrictions
key_articles.content: Women and minors under eighteen years of age shall not be employed in industrial work between 7:00 PM and 7:00 AM, subject to exceptions provided by decree. Night work for adult male workers shall be compensated at a higher rate.
key_articles.text_english: Night Work Restrictions: Women and minors under eighteen years of age shall not be employed in industrial work between 7:00 PM and 7:00 AM, subject to exceptions provided by decree. Night work for adult male workers shall be compensated at a higher rate.
key_articles.subject: Night Work Restrictions

key_articles.title: Weekly Rest
key_articles.content: Every employee is entitled to a weekly rest period of at least 36 consecutive hours, which shall normally include Sunday. The employer may fix the weekly rest day on a day other than Sunday for certain categories of work, provided the minimum rest period is observed.
key_articles.text_english: Weekly Rest: Every employee is entitled to a weekly rest period of at least 36 consecutive hours, which shall normally include Sunday. The employer may fix the weekly rest day on a day other than Sunday for certain categories of work, provided the minimum rest period is observed.
key_articles.subject: Weekly Rest

key_articles.title: Public Holidays
key_articles.content: Employees are entitled to paid leave on official public holidays as determined by the government. Work performed on public holidays shall be compensated at double the normal rate.
key_articles.text_english: Public Holidays: Employees are entitled to paid leave on official public holidays as determined by the government. Work performed on public holidays shall be compensated at double the normal rate.
key_articles.subject: Public Holidays

key_articles.title: Minimum Wage
key_articles.content: The minimum wage shall be fixed by decree of the Council of Ministers, taking into account the cost of living, the economic situation, and the needs of the worker and his family. The salary should not be less than the average of the official minimum salary. The minimum wage as fixed by the Government is 675,000 LBP (subject to periodic revision).
key_articles.text_english: Minimum Wage: The minimum wage shall be fixed by decree of the Council of Ministers, taking into account the cost of living, the economic situation, and the needs of the worker and his family. The salary should not be less than the average of the official minimum salary. The minimum wage as fixed by the Government is 675,000 LBP (subject to periodic revision).
key_articles.subject: Minimum Wage

key_articles.title: Payment of Wages
key_articles.content: Wages shall be paid at regular intervals not exceeding one month for monthly employees and one week for daily or piece-rate workers. Payment shall be made in the national currency at the workplace or through a bank transfer. Wages must be paid before any housing allowance that forms part of the remuneration.
key_articles.text_english: Payment of Wages: Wages shall be paid at regular intervals not exceeding one month for monthly employees and one week for daily or piece-rate workers. Payment shall be made in the national currency at the workplace or through a bank transfer. Wages must be paid before any housing allowance that forms part of the remuneration.
key_articles.subject: Payment of Wages

key_articles.title: Wage Deductions
key_articles.content: No deductions shall be made from an employee's wages except those provided by law, such as social security contributions, income tax, and amounts ordered by a court. Fines imposed by the employer shall not exceed five days' wages per month.
key_articles.text_english: Wage Deductions: No deductions shall be made from an employee's wages except those provided by law, such as social security contributions, income tax, and amounts ordered by a court. Fines imposed by the employer shall not exceed five days' wages per month.
key_articles.subject: Wage Deductions

key_articles.title: Equal Pay
key_articles.content: Women shall receive equal pay with men for equal work of the same nature and quality performed under the same conditions.
key_articles.text_english: Equal Pay: Women shall receive equal pay with men for equal work of the same nature and quality performed under the same conditions.
key_articles.subject: Equal Pay

key_articles.title: Annual Leave
key_articles.content: Every employee has the right, every year, to take fifteen days of paid annual leave if one year has passed from the date of the conclusion of the employment contract. Employers may choose the date for such leaves according to work circumstances. The employer cannot dismiss the employee or send him a warning or a notice during his annual leave.
key_articles.text_english: Annual Leave: Every employee has the right, every year, to take fifteen days of paid annual leave if one year has passed from the date of the conclusion of the employment contract. Employers may choose the date for such leaves according to work circumstances. The employer cannot dismiss the employee or send him a warning or a notice during his annual leave.
key_articles.subject: Annual Leave

key_articles.title: Sick Leave
key_articles.content: An employee who is unable to work due to illness or injury not related to employment shall be entitled to sick leave based on a medical report. The employer cannot dismiss or warn the employee during sick leave. The duration and compensation for sick leave is: half a month with full salary and half a month with half salary for employees with 3 months to 2 years of service; one month with full salary and one month with half salary for 2 to 4 years of service; one month and a half with full salary and one month and a half with half salary for 4 to 6 years of service; two months with full salary and two months with half salary for 6 to 10 years of service.
key_articles.text_english: Sick Leave: An employee who is unable to work due to illness or injury not related to employment shall be entitled to sick leave based on a medical report. The employer cannot dismiss or warn the employee during sick leave. The duration and compensation for sick leave is: half a month with full salary and half a month with half salary for employees with 3 months to 2 years of service; one month with full salary and one month with half salary for 2 to 4 years of service; one month and a half with full salary and one month and a half with half salary for 4 to 6 years of service; two months with full salary and two months with half salary for 6 to 10 years of service.
key_articles.subject: Sick Leave

key_articles.title: Maternity Leave
key_articles.content: A female employee is entitled to seven weeks of maternity leave with full pay, which may be taken before or after delivery. The employer shall not dismiss a female employee during her maternity leave or because of pregnancy. A nursing mother is entitled to one hour per day for nursing during the first year after birth.
key_articles.text_english: Maternity Leave: A female employee is entitled to seven weeks of maternity leave with full pay, which may be taken before or after delivery. The employer shall not dismiss a female employee during her maternity leave or because of pregnancy. A nursing mother is entitled to one hour per day for nursing during the first year after birth.
key_articles.subject: Maternity Leave

key_articles.title: Bereavement Leave
key_articles.content: An employee is entitled to two days of paid leave in case of the death of a family member (father, mother, children, or grandparents).
key_articles.text_english: Bereavement Leave: An employee is entitled to two days of paid leave in case of the death of a family member (father, mother, children, or grandparents).
key_articles.subject: Bereavement Leave

key_articles.title: Leave During Notice Period
key_articles.content: The employee has the right to leave work for one hour per day to search for another job during the notice period if any resignation or termination occurs.
key_articles.text_english: Leave During Notice Period: The employee has the right to leave work for one hour per day to search for another job during the notice period if any resignation or termination occurs.
key_articles.subject: Leave During Notice Period

key_articles.title: Employer's Obligation to Pay Salary
key_articles.content: The employer must pay salary weekly or monthly. Payment may be in cash or in kind. The employer must pay the employee their basic wage before any housing allowance that forms part of their remuneration.
key_articles.text_english: Employer's Obligation to Pay Salary: The employer must pay salary weekly or monthly. Payment may be in cash or in kind. The employer must pay the employee their basic wage before any housing allowance that forms part of their remuneration.
key_articles.subject: Employer's Obligation to Pay Salary

key_articles.title: Healthy and Safe Workplace
key_articles.content: The employer must provide a healthy workplace with no hazardous environment and safe equipment. The employer shall take all necessary precautions to protect the lives and health of employees.
key_articles.text_english: Healthy and Safe Workplace: The employer must provide a healthy workplace with no hazardous environment and safe equipment. The employer shall take all necessary precautions to protect the lives and health of employees.
key_articles.subject: Healthy and Safe Workplace

key_articles.title: Dignity and Respect
key_articles.content: The employer must treat the employee with dignity. No insult or harassment shall be directed at employees. The employer shall respect the personal dignity and freedom of the employee.
key_articles.text_english: Dignity and Respect: The employer must treat the employee with dignity. No insult or harassment shall be directed at employees. The employer shall respect the personal dignity and freedom of the employee.
key_articles.subject: Dignity and Respect

key_articles.title: Provision of Work and Tools
key_articles.content: The employer must allow the employee to do their job by providing access to the premises and supplying the pertinent tools needed to fulfill their tasks.
key_articles.text_english: Provision of Work and Tools: The employer must allow the employee to do their job by providing access to the premises and supplying the pertinent tools needed to fulfill their tasks.
key_articles.subject: Provision of Work and Tools

key_articles.title: Internal Work Policy
key_articles.content: An employer who has fifteen employees or more must establish an internal work policy (règlement intérieur) setting out the rules of discipline, working hours, leaves, and other working conditions. This policy must be approved by the Ministry of Labour.
key_articles.text_english: Internal Work Policy: An employer who has fifteen employees or more must establish an internal work policy (règlement intérieur) setting out the rules of discipline, working hours, leaves, and other working conditions. This policy must be approved by the Ministry of Labour.
key_articles.subject: Internal Work Policy

key_articles.title: Performance of Work
key_articles.content: The employee must perform the work as agreed in the employment contract and act as a prudent administrator in carrying out assigned duties.
key_articles.text_english: Performance of Work: The employee must perform the work as agreed in the employment contract and act as a prudent administrator in carrying out assigned duties.
key_articles.subject: Performance of Work

key_articles.title: Following Instructions
key_articles.content: The employee must follow the orders and instructions of the employer and work under the employer's supervision and direction.
key_articles.text_english: Following Instructions: The employee must follow the orders and instructions of the employer and work under the employer's supervision and direction.
key_articles.subject: Following Instructions

key_articles.title: Non-Competition
key_articles.content: The employee must refrain from competition with the employer during and after employment, subject to limitations of time and distance as may be agreed in the contract or required by law.
key_articles.text_english: Non-Competition: The employee must refrain from competition with the employer during and after employment, subject to limitations of time and distance as may be agreed in the contract or required by law.
key_articles.subject: Non-Competition

key_articles.title: Termination by Mutual Consent
key_articles.content: The employment contract may be terminated by the mutual consent of both parties. In this case, both parties decide to put an end to the employment contract by agreement.
key_articles.text_english: Termination by Mutual Consent: The employment contract may be terminated by the mutual consent of both parties. In this case, both parties decide to put an end to the employment contract by agreement.
key_articles.subject: Termination by Mutual Consent

key_articles.title: Termination by Force Majeure
key_articles.content: Any strong event (force majeure) which might happen to the employer, to the employee, or to the establishment, such as the reduction in the size of the establishment, substituting a line of production with another, or the permanent cessation of work, could lead to the termination of the employment contract.
key_articles.text_english: Termination by Force Majeure: Any strong event (force majeure) which might happen to the employer, to the employee, or to the establishment, such as the reduction in the size of the establishment, substituting a line of production with another, or the permanent cessation of work, could lead to the termination of the employment contract.
key_articles.subject: Termination by Force Majeure

key_articles.title: Termination by Employer Without Indemnity
key_articles.content: The employer may terminate the employment contract without indemnity in the following cases: (a) If the employee has assumed a nationality that is not his own; (b) If the period of work was set as a trial and the employer refused the employee within the three-month time limit; (c) If the employee commits or causes any damage to the employer, provided the employer documents this in writing and submits it to the Labour Ministry within three days; (d) If the employee has been absent, with no legal excuse, for more than fifteen days in one year, or for seven consecutive days; (e) If the employee was imprisoned for one year or more for a felony or misdemeanor at or through work; (f) If the employee attacked the employer or the manager at work.
key_articles.text_english: Termination by Employer Without Indemnity: The employer may terminate the employment contract without indemnity in the following cases: (a) If the employee has assumed a nationality that is not his own; (b) If the period of work was set as a trial and the employer refused the employee within the three-month time limit; (c) If the employee commits or causes any damage to the employer, provided the employer documents this in writing and submits it to the Labour Ministry within three days; (d) If the employee has been absent, with no legal excuse, for more than fifteen days in one year, or for seven consecutive days; (e) If the employee was imprisoned for one year or more for a felony or misdemeanor at or through work; (f) If the employee attacked the employer or the manager at work.
key_articles.subject: Termination by Employer Without Indemnity

key_articles.title: Termination by Employee
key_articles.content: The employee has the right to leave work before the end of the employment contract in the following cases: (a) If the employer or his representative misleads the employee about the conditions of work, within thirty days of starting work; (b) If the employer fails to execute his obligations; (c) If the employer commits an unethical act against the employee or a member of his family; (d) If the employer or his representative commits a violent act against the employee.
key_articles.text_english: Termination by Employee: The employee has the right to leave work before the end of the employment contract in the following cases: (a) If the employer or his representative misleads the employee about the conditions of work, within thirty days of starting work; (b) If the employer fails to execute his obligations; (c) If the employer commits an unethical act against the employee or a member of his family; (d) If the employer or his representative commits a violent act against the employee.
key_articles.subject: Termination by Employee

key_articles.title: Abusive Dismissal
key_articles.content: A dismissal is considered abusive (without just reason) when it is: (a) Not related to the quality of work; (b) Due to union membership; (c) Due to running for or being elected to union office; (d) Due to submitting a complaint to the Labour Ministry regarding implementation of labor law or filing a complaint against the employer; (e) Due to the employee exercising personal freedoms within the law. The damaged party may claim before the Labor Council within one month from knowledge of the dismissal and may use all kinds of proof. The Labor Council must take its decision within three months.
key_articles.text_english: Abusive Dismissal: A dismissal is considered abusive (without just reason) when it is: (a) Not related to the quality of work; (b) Due to union membership; (c) Due to running for or being elected to union office; (d) Due to submitting a complaint to the Labour Ministry regarding implementation of labor law or filing a complaint against the employer; (e) Due to the employee exercising personal freedoms within the law. The damaged party may claim before the Labor Council within one month from knowledge of the dismissal and may use all kinds of proof. The Labor Council must take its decision within three months.
key_articles.subject: Abusive Dismissal

key_articles.title: End-of-Service Indemnity
key_articles.content: The employer must pay the dismissed employee a remuneration equivalent to the salary of one month for every year worked, and the salary of half a month if the period of work was less than one year. An employee who has reached the age of 60 or who has completed 25 years of service at the same job may request dismissal and benefit from the leave indemnity.
key_articles.text_english: End-of-Service Indemnity: The employer must pay the dismissed employee a remuneration equivalent to the salary of one month for every year worked, and the salary of half a month if the period of work was less than one year. An employee who has reached the age of 60 or who has completed 25 years of service at the same job may request dismissal and benefit from the leave indemnity.
key_articles.subject: End-of-Service Indemnity

key_articles.title: Warning and Infringement Procedure
key_articles.content: If the employee, despite a warning, has committed three infringements against the internal regulations within one year, the employer may terminate the contract without indemnity. The employer must document each infringement in writing and submit it to the Labour Ministry within three days from the date of becoming aware of the infringement.
key_articles.text_english: Warning and Infringement Procedure: If the employee, despite a warning, has committed three infringements against the internal regulations within one year, the employer may terminate the contract without indemnity. The employer must document each infringement in writing and submit it to the Labour Ministry within three days from the date of becoming aware of the infringement.
key_articles.subject: Warning and Infringement Procedure

key_articles.title: Labor Councils (Judicial Competency)
key_articles.content: In each district (Mouhafaza), there is one or more Labor Council which treats disputes arising between employers and employees. The Labor Council is composed of: (1) A judge from the 11th degree and above as president; (2) Two members: one employee representative and one employer representative (with two alternates for absences); (3) A Government Commissioner of the 3rd degree.
key_articles.text_english: Labor Councils (Judicial Competency): In each district (Mouhafaza), there is one or more Labor Council which treats disputes arising between employers and employees. The Labor Council is composed of: (1) A judge from the 11th degree and above as president; (2) Two members: one employee representative and one employer representative (with two alternates for absences); (3) A Government Commissioner of the 3rd degree.
key_articles.subject: Labor Councils (Judicial Competency)

key_articles.title: Labor Council Procedures
key_articles.content: The Labor Council shall attempt to reconcile the parties before proceeding to adjudicate the dispute. If reconciliation fails, the Council shall render a decision. For abusive dismissal claims, the Council must take its decision within three months.
key_articles.text_english: Labor Council Procedures: The Labor Council shall attempt to reconcile the parties before proceeding to adjudicate the dispute. If reconciliation fails, the Council shall render a decision. For abusive dismissal claims, the Council must take its decision within three months.
key_articles.subject: Labor Council Procedures

key_articles.title: Prohibition of Child Labour
key_articles.content: Children under the age of 14 years shall not be employed in any work. Children between 14 and 18 years may be employed only in light work that is not harmful to their health, growth, or education, and only with the authorization of the Ministry of Labour.
key_articles.text_english: Prohibition of Child Labour: Children under the age of 14 years shall not be employed in any work. Children between 14 and 18 years may be employed only in light work that is not harmful to their health, growth, or education, and only with the authorization of the Ministry of Labour.
key_articles.subject: Prohibition of Child Labour

key_articles.title: Restrictions on Women's Employment
key_articles.content: Women shall not be employed in work that is dangerous, unhealthy, or morally harmful as defined by decree. Pregnant women shall not be required to perform work that may endanger their health or that of the child.
key_articles.text_english: Restrictions on Women's Employment: Women shall not be employed in work that is dangerous, unhealthy, or morally harmful as defined by decree. Pregnant women shall not be required to perform work that may endanger their health or that of the child.
key_articles.subject: Restrictions on Women's Employment

key_articles.title: Equal Treatment
key_articles.content: Employers shall ensure equal treatment of employees regardless of sex, origin, or belief in matters of hiring, working conditions, promotion, wages, and termination.
key_articles.text_english: Equal Treatment: Employers shall ensure equal treatment of employees regardless of sex, origin, or belief in matters of hiring, working conditions, promotion, wages, and termination.
key_articles.subject: Equal Treatment

key_articles.title: Trade Unions
key_articles.content: Workers and employers have the right to form and join trade unions for the defense of their professional interests. Trade unions must be registered with the Ministry of Labour and must have at least 15 members.
key_articles.text_english: Trade Unions: Workers and employers have the right to form and join trade unions for the defense of their professional interests. Trade unions must be registered with the Ministry of Labour and must have at least 15 members.
key_articles.subject: Trade Unions

key_articles.title: Collective Bargaining
key_articles.content: Employers and trade unions may negotiate collective labor agreements establishing conditions of employment that are more favorable than those provided by law. Collective agreements must be in writing and registered with the Ministry of Labour.
key_articles.text_english: Collective Bargaining: Employers and trade unions may negotiate collective labor agreements establishing conditions of employment that are more favorable than those provided by law. Collective agreements must be in writing and registered with the Ministry of Labour.
key_articles.subject: Collective Bargaining

key_articles.title: Right to Strike
key_articles.content: Workers have the right to strike as a means of defending their professional interests, provided that conciliation and mediation procedures have been exhausted. Strikes must be peaceful and must not involve violence or occupation of premises.
key_articles.text_english: Right to Strike: Workers have the right to strike as a means of defending their professional interests, provided that conciliation and mediation procedures have been exhausted. Strikes must be peaceful and must not involve violence or occupation of premises.
key_articles.subject: Right to Strike

key_articles.title: Lock-out
key_articles.content: Employers may resort to lock-out only after conciliation and mediation procedures have been exhausted. Lock-out must comply with the provisions of the Code of Collective Labor Agreements.
key_articles.text_english: Lock-out: Employers may resort to lock-out only after conciliation and mediation procedures have been exhausted. Lock-out must comply with the provisions of the Code of Collective Labor Agreements.
key_articles.subject: Lock-out

key_articles.title: Work-Related Injuries
key_articles.content: Employers are liable for injuries and occupational diseases suffered by employees in the course of or because of their work. Compensation for work-related injuries is governed by the Code of Occupational Injuries of 1983.
key_articles.text_english: Work-Related Injuries: Employers are liable for injuries and occupational diseases suffered by employees in the course of or because of their work. Compensation for work-related injuries is governed by the Code of Occupational Injuries of 1983.
key_articles.subject: Work-Related Injuries

key_articles.title: Social Security Contributions
key_articles.content: Employers and employees are required to contribute to the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) as provided by the Code of Social Security of 1963. The NSSF provides benefits for sickness, maternity, family allowances, and end-of-service indemnity.
key_articles.text_english: Social Security Contributions: Employers and employees are required to contribute to the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) as provided by the Code of Social Security of 1963. The NSSF provides benefits for sickness, maternity, family allowances, and end-of-service indemnity.
key_articles.subject: Social Security Contributions

key_articles.title: Employment of Foreigners
key_articles.content: Foreign nationals may be employed in Lebanon only after obtaining a work permit from the Ministry of Labour. The work permit is granted based on the principle of priority for Lebanese workers and is subject to annual renewal.
key_articles.text_english: Employment of Foreigners: Foreign nationals may be employed in Lebanon only after obtaining a work permit from the Ministry of Labour. The work permit is granted based on the principle of priority for Lebanese workers and is subject to annual renewal.
key_articles.subject: Employment of Foreigners

key_articles.title: Reciprocity Principle
key_articles.content: The employment of foreign workers is subject to reciprocity with the worker's country of origin. The Ministry of Labour may impose conditions on the employment of foreigners to protect the national labor market.
key_articles.text_english: Reciprocity Principle: The employment of foreign workers is subject to reciprocity with the worker's country of origin. The Ministry of Labour may impose conditions on the employment of foreigners to protect the national labor market.
key_articles.subject: Reciprocity Principle

key_articles.title: Labour Inspection
key_articles.content: The Ministry of Labour shall appoint labour inspectors to supervise the implementation of this Code. Labour inspectors have the right to enter any establishment at any time to verify compliance with labor laws and regulations.
key_articles.text_english: Labour Inspection: The Ministry of Labour shall appoint labour inspectors to supervise the implementation of this Code. Labour inspectors have the right to enter any establishment at any time to verify compliance with labor laws and regulations.
key_articles.subject: Labour Inspection

key_articles.title: Penalties
key_articles.content: Any employer who violates the provisions of this Code shall be liable to fines as determined by law. Repeated violations may result in closure of the establishment by order of the Ministry of Labour.
key_articles.text_english: Penalties: Any employer who violates the provisions of this Code shall be liable to fines as determined by law. Repeated violations may result in closure of the establishment by order of the Ministry of Labour.
key_articles.subject: Penalties

key_articles.title: Transfer of Enterprise
key_articles.content: In the event of transfer of an enterprise by sale, merger, or succession, all employment contracts in force at the time of transfer shall remain binding on the new employer. Employees shall retain their rights and seniority.
key_articles.text_english: Transfer of Enterprise: In the event of transfer of an enterprise by sale, merger, or succession, all employment contracts in force at the time of transfer shall remain binding on the new employer. Employees shall retain their rights and seniority.
key_articles.subject: Transfer of Enterprise

key_articles.title: Employer's Certificate
key_articles.content: Upon termination of employment, the employer must provide the employee with a certificate of employment indicating the dates of commencement and termination, the nature of the work performed, and the last salary received. The employer may not include any unfavorable remarks in the certificate.

The employer may not include any unfavorable remarks in the certificate.
key_articles.subject: Employer's Certificate

key_articles.title: Workplace Register
key_articles.content: Every employer must maintain a register of employees indicating their names, nationalities, dates of engagement, wages, and other particulars as required by regulation.
key_articles.text_english: Workplace Register: Every employer must maintain a register of employees indicating their names, nationalities, dates of engagement, wages, and other particulars as required by regulation.
key_articles.subject: Workplace Register

key_articles.title: Apprenticeship
key_articles.content: An apprenticeship contract is a contract whereby an employer undertakes to provide vocational training to an apprentice who, in return, undertakes to work for the employer during the training period. The contract must be in writing and registered with the Ministry of Labour.

The contract must be in writing and registered with the Ministry of Labour.
key_articles.subject: Apprenticeship

key_articles.title: Non-Discrimination
key_articles.content: No employer may discriminate between employees on the basis of sex, origin, religion, or belief in any aspect of employment, including recruitment, wages, working conditions, promotion, and termination.

key_articles.subject: Non-Discrimination
